zh: 6. 中世纪的哲学
en: 6. Philosophy in the Middle Ages

zh: 随着西罗马帝国在五世纪的崩溃，欧洲大部分地区进入了一个被称为“黑暗时代”的野蛮阶段，其特征是文化的悲剧性衰落。希腊人和罗马人在艺术、科学和哲学领域取得的所有巨大成就，在数百年的时间里都付诸东流。人类不得不经历一条长达近1000 年的痛苦道路，才能重新找回这些成就。
en: Following the collapse of the Western Roman Empire in the fifth century, most of Europe entered a stage of barbarism known as the Dark Ages which was characterised by a tragic decline of culture. All the enormous advances made by the Greeks and the Romans in the spheres of art, science and philosophy were lost for hundreds of years. Humanity would have to go through a painful path lasting almost 1,000 years to recover them again.

zh: 渐渐地，一种新的社会形态从旧制度的废墟中应运而生，其基础是对农民的剥削——这些农民虽不再是奴隶，却在世俗领主和宗教领主的统治下被束缚于土地之上。社会金字塔式的结构反映了这种统治关系，其中包含一套针对所谓“天然上级”的僵硬义务与权利体系。然而，作为一切基础的根本义务，是农奴必须为其领主和主人提供无偿劳动服务。这正是这种社会形态区别于其之前的将奴隶当作财产的奴隶制及其之后的资本主义之处。整个制度由教会赋予神圣性；教会掌握着巨大权力，其自身也按类似的等级体系组织起来。
en: Gradually, a new form of society emerged from the wreckage of the old system, based on the exploitation of a peasantry who were no longer slaves, but were tied to the land under the domination of temporal and spiritual lords. The pyramidal structure of society reflected this domination, with a rigid system of alleged duties and rights to one’s ‘natural superiors’. The fundamental duty, however, upon which everything else depended, was the duty of the serf to provide free labour service for his lord and master. This is what distinguishes this form of society from both chattel slavery, which came before it, and capitalism, which followed it. The whole system was sanctified by the Church, which wielded immense power, and was organised along similar hierarchical lines.

zh: 封建制度所特有的僵硬社会等级制度，在教会的固定教条中找到了意识形态上的体现，这些教条要求人们根据对神圣经文的官方解释给予不加质疑的服从。教会教父们摒弃理性，宣扬盲目信仰，这可概括为据称出自德尔图良的那句名言：“Credo, quia absurdum est”——“我信，正因其荒谬”。科学则被视为可疑之物，是异教的遗产。
en: The rigid social hierarchy that characterised the feudal system found an ideological expression in the fixed dogmas of the Church, which demanded unquestioning obedience based on the official interpretation of the sacred texts. In place of reason, the Church Fathers preached blind faith, summed up in the celebrated phrase attributed to Tertullian, “Credo, quia absurdum est” – “I believe because it is absurd”. Science was looked on as suspicious, a heritage of paganism.

zh: 古希腊哲学的遗产一度失传，直到十二世纪才在西欧部分复兴。这种状况不利于思想和科学的发展。J. D. 伯纳尔写道：
en: The heritage of classical Greek philosophy was lost, and only partially revived in Western Europe in the twelfth century. Such a situation was not conducive to the development of thought and science. J. D. Bernal writes:

zh: 封建生产条件将对实用科学的需求降至最低。直到中世纪后期，随着贸易和航海催生出新的需求，这种需求才得以回升。智力活动转向了其他方向，并在很大程度上服务于文明中一个彻底崭新的特征——有组织的宗教信仰。
en: The conditions of feudal production reduced the demand for useful science to a minimum. It was not to increase again till trade and navigation created new needs in the later Middle Ages. Intellectual effort was to go in other directions and largely in the service of a radically new feature of civilisation – organised religious faiths.

zh: 据福布斯和迪克斯特胡伊斯所述：
en: According to Forbes and Dijksterhuis:

zh: 总体而言，基督教在其诞生的最初几个世纪里并不利于科学探索。由于科学源于异教，因此备受怀疑；此外，当时盛行一种观念，认为若深入探究自然的奥秘，超出《圣经》所允许的范围以及理解这些经文所需的程度，对基督徒的精神福祉并无裨益。
en: Generally speaking it may be said that during the first centuries of its existence Christianity was not conducive to scientific pursuits. Science was regarded with suspicion because of its pagan origin; moreover, the ideal prevailed that it was not advisable for the spiritual welfare of Christians to penetrate more deeply into the secrets of nature than was made possible by the Holy Scriptures and than was required to understand these.

zh: 当古典文化的残余最终传入西欧时，是以从阿拉伯语转译而来的译本形式出现的。正如我们在上一章所见，阿拉伯人在征服北非和西班牙直至比利牛斯山脉的过程中展现出的巨大活力，与其对被征服民族文化所采取的明智而灵活的态度相得益彰，这与基督徒在收复安达卢斯后所表现出的无知野蛮形成了鲜明对比。几个世纪以来，西班牙的伊斯兰大学，尤其是科尔多瓦的大学，是西欧唯一真正的学术中心——若排除爱尔兰的话，该地因地处偏远而始终游离于主流之外。阿拉伯人在众多领域取得了巨大进步——包括数学、天文学、地理学、医学、光学和化学，以及重要的技术进步，这体现在那些被基督徒肆意破坏的庞大灌溉工程上。但这些知识渗透到西欧却花了数百年时间。
en: When the remnants of classical culture eventually reached Western Europe, it was in translations from Arabic. As we have seen in the previous chapter, the great energy shown by the Arabs in conquering North Africa and Spain right up to the Pyrenees was matched by their intelligent and flexible attitude to the culture of the conquered peoples, in marked contrast to the ignorant barbarism displayed by the Christians after the reconquest of Al-Andalus. For centuries, the Islamic universities in Spain, especially the one at Córdoba, were the only real centres of learning in Western Europe, if we exclude Ireland, which, because of its remoteness, remained outside the mainstream. The Arabs made great advances in a whole number of fields – mathematics, astronomy, geography, medicine, optics and chemistry, as well as important technological advances, shown by the vast irrigation schemes which were wantonly destroyed by the Christians. But it took hundreds of years for this knowledge to percolate through to Western Europe.

zh: 由于教会对文化的垄断，所有智力活动都必须通过教会进行。几个世纪以来，教育仅限于修道院，并受到教会官僚机构的严格控制。对于中世纪的经院学者——即官方知识分子——而言，哲学是“神学的婢女”。科学被压缩到最低限度：“算术仅限于计数；几何学仅限于欧几里得的前三卷；天文学几乎仅止于历法和如何计算复活节日期；而物理学则远离实际，而且是柏拉图式的。”
人们对科学研究和实验毫无兴趣。
en: Because of the Church’s monopoly on culture, all intellectual life had to be channelled through it. For centuries, education was confined to the monasteries under the strict control of the Church officialdom. For the medieval Schoolmen – or Scholastics, as the official intelligentsia were called – philosophy was the “handmaiden of theology.” Science was reduced to a bare minimum: “Arithmetic was numeration; geometry the first three books of Euclid; astronomy hardly got past the calendar and how to compute the date of Easter; and the physics were very remote and Platonic.”
No interest was shown in scientific research and experiment.

zh: 实在论与唯名论：共相问题
en: REALISM AND NOMINALISM: THE QUESTION OF UNIVERSALS

zh: 中世纪神权政治的思想支柱是希波的圣奥古斯丁（公元354—430 年）的思想，他是“黑暗时代”最具影响力的哲学家。奥古斯丁立足于新柏拉图主义思想中最反动的要素。他的哲学是基督教神秘主义与一种粗糙且贫乏的柏拉图唯心主义的混合体。由于奥古斯丁思想是罗马天主教会的主要意识形态，任何反对它的观点都被视为本质上的异端并遭到迫害。
en: The ideological pillar of mediaeval theocracy was the ideas of St Augustine of Hippo (354-430 AD), the most influential philosopher of the Dark Ages. Augustine based himself on the most reactionary elements of neoplatonist thought. His philosophy was a mix of Christian mysticism and a crude and impoverished form of Platonic idealism. As the main ideology of the Roman Catholic Church, any and all opposition to Augustinian thought was deemed inherently heretical and persecuted.

zh: 效法柏拉图，奥古斯丁认为所有存在物都是按照普遍的原型形成的，这些原型是超越我们物质世界而真实存在的实体。在柏拉图的体系中，这些原型——或如他所称的“理念”——存在于另一个领域，人类只能通过纯粹的哲学思考才能触及。然而对于奥古斯丁而言，这些原型——或如他所称的“理则”——存在于神的思想之中，人类只能通过信仰才能触及。
en: Following Plato, Augustine believed that all beings were formed in accordance to universal archetypes, which are real entities existing beyond our physical world. In Plato’s system, these archetypes – or ‘forms’, as he called them – exist in a different realm which can only be accessed by humans by way of pure philosophical thought. For Augustine, however, the archetypes – or ‘reasons’, as he called them – exist in the divine mind and are only accessible to humans by way of faith.

zh: 奥古斯丁的“共相”理论构成了中世纪哲学中被冠以“实在论”这一易引起混淆的名称这一思潮的基础。实在论者追随奥古斯丁和柏拉图，认为我们所拥有的“人”、“动物”、“树”、“岩石”等一般概念，是基于真实存在且恒常不变的原型事物。这些共相进而构成了我们生活中所体验到的那些个别且不断变化的“人”、“动物”、“树”和“岩石”的基础。但我们如何认识这些共相呢？根据奥古斯丁的观点，事物的真正本质存在于上帝的意念之中。因此，在人间寻找它们毫无意义：相反，我们应当将目光投向上帝所在的天国。
en: Augustine’s theory of universals lay at the base of the trend in mediaeval philosophy confusingly called Realism. The Realists, following Augustine and Plato, believed that the general concepts that we have, such as ‘man’, ‘animal’, ‘tree’, ‘rock’ etc., are based on real existing and unchanging archetypal things. These universals in turn form the basis of the singular and changing men, animals, trees and rocks that we experience in life. But how do we get to know these universals? According to Augustine, it is in God’s mind that the true essence of things can be found. Hence, there is no point in looking for them on earth: rather, we should direct our gaze to the heavens where God resides.

zh: 奥古斯丁的世界观中没有科学或探究的余地，最终甚至连理性思考也无立足之地。在此，理智是被动的，仅凭借信仰来接受知识。根据基督教教义，奥古斯丁认为一切物质和世俗之物本质上都是低等的，甚至是罪恶的。男女（尤其是女性）的身体是罪的载体，应当被视为可憎之物。真正的生活始于死亡的瞬间，那时灵魂终于从物质的牢笼中获得解放。从这一视角来看，真理无法在物质世界中被发现，这便顺理成章：“……任何真正意义上的真理，都不应指望从肉体的感官中获得。”
en: Augustine’s world view leaves no room for science or investigation, and ultimately not even for rational thought. Here the intellect is passive and merely receives knowledge on grounds of its faith. In accordance with Christian doctrine, Augustine considered all material and earthly things to be inherently inferior, and even sinful. The bodies of men and women (particularly women) were objects of sin, to be regarded with abhorrence. Real life began at the moment of death, when the soul was finally freed from its material prison. From this point of view, it was quite natural that truth was not to be found in the material world: “… truth in any genuine sense is not something to be expected from the bodily senses.”

zh: 因此，客观世界充其量只是次要的，而我们的感官在引导我们走向真理方面毫无用处。“Crede, ut intelligas”——“先信，然后才能理解”——奥古斯丁曾有此名言。真理仅存于上帝那静止且永恒不变的心智之中，而上帝又会以其真理照亮我们的心智——前提是我们足够“纯洁”且“圣洁”。因此，对一切真理的最终裁决权掌握在至圣中的至圣者手中：即天主教会的神职精英。这一认识论被称为“神圣光照论”，它与奥古斯丁实在论共同为中世纪反动思潮奠定了哲学基础。
en: Accordingly, the objective world is, at best, of a secondary importance, and our senses are useless in leading us to the truth. “Crede, ut intelligas” – “Believe so that you may understand” – Augustine famously said. Truth is only to be found in the static and immutable mind of God, who in turn illuminates our minds with his truth – that is, if we are ‘pure’ and ‘holy’ enough. Thus, the ultimate judgement of all truth is placed in the hands of the holiest of holies: the clerical elite of the Catholic Church. This theory of knowledge was known as the theory of Divine Illumination and, along with Augustinian Realism, it laid the philosophical foundation of mediaeval reaction.

zh: 这一思想学派在欧洲称霸了数百年，当时科学与文化似乎已失去一切希望。然而，在表面之下，历史的鼹鼠仍在默默掘进。生产力正在发展——尽管非常缓慢——科学技术也随之发展。
en: This school of thought reigned supreme in Europe for hundreds of years, when all hope for science and culture appeared to be lost. However, underneath the surface, the mole of history was still burrowing away. The productive forces were developing – albeit very slowly – and along with them science and technology.

zh: 在十二世纪和十三世纪，欧洲的封建社会达到了顶峰。几乎所有的耕地都被利用起来，土地生产力以及农业总产量都达到了最高水平。在此基础上，人口不断增长，中世纪早期人口稀少的大陆逐渐演变为由众多小镇乃至少数大城市组成的庞大网络。巴黎、佛罗伦萨、威尼斯和热那亚的人口达到约10 万，而伦敦、根特和科隆则达到约5 万。国家机器和城市机构日益庞大，对专业人才的需求随之增加。传统的修道院教育机构已无法满足需求。因此，我们见证了大学的兴起，在那里，法学和医学独立于神学而发展。
en: In the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, feudal society in Europe was reaching its peak. Almost all arable land was in use and the productivity of the land, as well as the total yield of agriculture, was at its highest. On this basis, the population increased and the sparsely populated continent of the early mediaeval period gave way to a vast network of small towns, and even a few cities. Paris, Florence, Venice and Genoa reached populations of around 100,000, while London, Ghent and Cologne reached around 50,000. The state apparatus and urban institutions swelled, and with them the need for professionals. The old monastic education institutions were no longer sufficient. Hence, we witness the rise of the universities, where law and medical science developed separately from theology.

zh: 在修道院的教育传统中，学生不被允许发言，甚至不能提问。但在大学里，情况则大不相同。在这里，主要的学习方法之一是“辩论”，即围绕神学主题进行的公开辩论。另一门与辩论同时发展起来的重要学科是辩证法，即理性论证的学科。这些辩论所涉及的主题仍然极具神秘主义和宗教色彩。不允许偏离基督教权威。唯一的例外是柏拉图和亚里士多德，以及对他们的注释——教会不得不勉强接受这些内容。
en: In the monastic educational tradition, students were not allowed to speak, not even to ask questions. But in the universities matters were quite different. Here, one of the main methods of learning was through ‘disputations’, which were open public debates about theological topics. Another important discipline, which developed in conjunction with the disputations, was dialectics, the discipline of rational argument. The topics in question in these debates were still highly mystical and religious. Departure from Christian authority was not allowed. The exceptions were Plato and Aristotle, along with commentaries on these, which the Church reluctantly had to accept.

zh: 尽管如此，这种思想上的部分解放使哲学重获新生。在关于“天使是个体还是种”、“上帝是单纯的还是复合的”以及“神圣意识中的共相”等议题的辩论之下，中世纪经院哲学家们正在慢慢重新发现哲学。
en: Nevertheless, this partial liberation of ideas gave philosophy a new lease on life. Underneath debates on such things as whether angels are individuals or a species, whether God is simple or complex, and the question of the Universals in the divine mind, the mediaeval Schoolmen were slowly rediscovering philosophy.

zh: 与此同时，另一件重要事件为这一发展提供了强有力的推动力。为了充实大学的课程设置——特别是文学院和医学院的课程——人们开始认真致力于将科学和哲学著作从阿拉伯语翻译成拉丁语。几乎所有的古希腊经典作品都在“黑暗时代”中失传了，但如今它们开始与阿拉伯科学家和哲学家的著作一起重返欧洲。
en: Meanwhile, another important event gave a major impulse to this development. To fill the curriculums in the universities, in particular for the arts faculties and the medical sciences, a serious endeavour was made to translate scientific and philosophical texts from Arabic into Latin. Almost all of the classical Greek works had been lost during the Dark Ages, but now they started finding their way back into Europe, along with works by Arabic scientists and philosophers.

zh: 这标志着哲学与科学从宗教中分离出来的进程刚刚拉开序幕。数百年来，笼罩在欧洲上空的黑暗中首次透出了一丝曙光。在哲学领域，矛盾开始层出不穷，而旧有的奥古斯丁范式已无法加以解释。
en: This was the early beginning of the process of separation of philosophy and science from religion. For the first time in hundreds of years, a glimmer of light could be seen in the darkness that had covered Europe. In philosophy, contradictions began to pile up that the old Augustinian paradigm could not account for.

zh: 与旧有道路——即所谓的“via antiqua”（古道）——的首次决裂，源自法国经院哲学家彼得·阿伯拉尔（1079—1142）。阿伯拉尔因与当时另一位杰出思想家爱洛伊丝的悲情恋事而闻名。这往往让人忽略了一个事实：他是一位富有创新精神且勇敢的思想家，因被誉为当时最杰出的辩论家和辩证法大师而在整个欧洲声名远扬。
en: The first break with the old way – via antiqua, as it was called – came from the French scholastic, Peter Abelard (1079-1142). Abelard is known for his tragic love life with another prominent thinker of the time, Heloïse. This often distracts from the fact that he was an innovative and courageous thinker, renowned across Europe for being the most formidable debater and dialectician of his time.

zh: 阿伯拉尔还是“唯名论”的奠基人。这一学派与“实在论”相对立，主张“共相”并不作为真实事物存在于上帝的意识中，也不存在于任何其他地方。他以亚里士多德的理论和严谨的逻辑为基础，驳斥了奥古斯丁的实在论，并证明了共相并不是那种真实存在、由世间个别事物分有或以其他方式反映的原型。相反，他坚持认为所有存在都是个体的：一个人就是那个特定的人，一块石头也仅仅是一块特定的石头。
en: Abelard was also the father of Nominalism, the school of thought that, as opposed to Realism, claimed that universals do not exist as real things in the mind of God or anywhere else. Basing himself on Aristotle and a meticulous logic, he rejected Augustinian Realism and proved that universals are not really existing archetypes in which singular things in the world participate or otherwise reflect. Rather, he maintained that all beings are singular: a man is just that man, and a rock is just that, a particular rock.

zh: 他认为，“人”、“动物”等概念仅仅是人类通过约定俗成演变而来的词语，用于指代现实世界中的事物，但这些概念在人类意识之外并不具有现实性。据阿伯拉尔所言，物质对象的形式——除上帝、天使和人类之外——仅仅是土、气、火、水这四种元素不同组合的结果。在这个等式中，共相并不作为独立的组成部分出现。
en: He held that concepts such as man, animal, etc., are just words that humans have evolved by convention to signify things in the real world, but which have no reality beyond human consciousness. According to Abelard, the form of material objects – apart from God, angels and human beings – is merely the result of different combinations of the four elements: earth, air, fire and water. Universals do not figure as a separate compound in this equation.

zh: 但这并不意味着阿伯拉尔认为我们的一般普遍概念与任何事物都不对应。在他看来，个别事物具有相似的本质。例如，产卵和长有翅膀是鸟类的本质——这是我们可以从对鸟类的经验中推导出来的。他说，我们的普遍词语对应于他所说的事物的“状态”——这个术语我们可以广义地理解为事物的存在方式或其内在规律。因此，例如动物所共有的特征并非任意而为，而是反映了导致动物产生的相似自然过程。
en: But this does not mean that Abelard thought that our general universal concepts do not correspond to anything at all. According to him, singular things have similar natures. It is in the nature of birds, for instance, to lay eggs and to have wings – something we can deduce from our experience of them. Our universal words, he said, correspond to what he calls the ‘statuses’ of things – a term we can broadly interpret to mean their mode of existence or their inner lawfulness. Hence, the shared features of say, animals, are not arbitrary. They reflect the similar natural processes that lead to the creation of animals.

zh: 这与传统的教会信仰截然不同，几乎没有给超自然现象留下任何空间。据阿伯拉尔所言，上帝在此过程中唯一的作用，是在时间的开端定义这些自然法则。这也意味着，人类获取知识并不需要神圣光照。相反，我们的知识是通过感官体验，以及我们对现实世界中现象进行抽象和概括的能力而获得的。
en: This is a radical departure from conventional Church beliefs and leaves little room for the supernatural. The only role God has in this process, according to Abelard, is to define these laws of nature at the inception of time. It also means that no divine illumination is needed for humans to acquire knowledge. Rather, our knowledge is acquired by way of our sense experiences, as well as our ability to abstract and generalise the phenomena that we meet in the real world.

zh: 这种偏离官方教义的观点在天主教当局中引发了强烈愤怒，但阿伯拉尔顽强地坚持了自己的立场。尽管敌人竭力试图让他噤声，他仍对通过神圣光照获取知识的理论给予了致命一击。在他之后，知识通过感官经验和抽象思维获得这一观点几乎被普遍接受。后来，这将导致奥古斯丁思想的彻底瓦解。
en: This deviation from the official doctrines caused a lot of anger among the Catholic officialdom, but Abelard stubbornly stood his ground. In spite of all the attempts of his enemies to shut him up, he dealt a mortal blow to the theory of knowledge via divine illumination. After his time, it was almost universally accepted that knowledge is acquired via sense experience and abstraction. Later on, this would lead to the complete unravelling of Augustinian thought.

zh: 阿伯拉尔是一位虔诚的基督徒，但他更忠于自己的信念和理性思考，这使他一再与教会发生冲突。由于多次偏离官方教义，阿伯拉尔曾多次遭到教会当局的迫害、绝罚，并被定为异端。有一次，他的著作甚至被下令焚毁，多亏一位富有的赞助人出面干预，才侥幸逃过这一劫。尽管如此，阿伯拉尔在年轻学生中依然极具人气，成千上万的学生蜂拥而至，聆听他的讲座。
en: Abelard was a devout Christian, but he was more dedicated to his convictions and rational thought, something which time and time again brought him into conflict with the Church. For his many deviations from the official doctrines, Abelard was persecuted, excommunicated and condemned as a heretic on several occasions by ecclesiastic authorities. At one point, his books were ordered to be burned, and only narrowly escaped that fate thanks to the intervention of a wealthy patron. Nevertheless, Abelard remained hugely popular with young students, who flocked to his lectures in their thousands.

zh: 虽然阿伯拉尔绝非革命者，但他的思想被视为对天主教会对中世纪社会的意识形态垄断构成了存在性威胁。但教会这场斗争注定要失败。阿伯拉尔预见了十三世纪的发展趋势——那时，奥古斯丁式的旧思想体系将进入彻底衰落的时期。这一发展进程的最后一个关键环节，是亚里士多德著作的复兴，这些著作在修道院教育传统中早已被遗忘。
en: While Abelard was by no means a revolutionary, his ideas were seen as an existential threat to the ideological stranglehold of the Catholic Church on medieval society. But the Church was fighting a losing battle. Abelard anticipated the developments of the thirteenth century, where the old way of Augustinian thought entered a period of definitive decline. The final element in this development was the recovery of Aristotle’s works, which had long been forgotten in the monastic educational tradition.

zh: 在十二世纪之前，只有亚里士多德的《范畴论》和《论解释》有拉丁文译本，而这两部恰恰是亚里士多德最平庸的作品。然而到了十三世纪中叶，他现存的几乎所有著作都已从阿拉伯语翻译成拉丁语，同时还包括了伊本·西那等伊斯兰思想家——尤其是阿威罗伊——的注释。事实上，阿威罗伊已成为解读亚里士多德的主要向导，以至于当人们称亚里士多德为“哲学家”时，阿威罗伊则被称为“注释家”。基于阿威罗伊的著述，经院哲学家们之中开始形成一种激进的亚里士多德主义思潮。
en: Prior to the twelfth century, only Aristotle’s Categories and On Interpretation were available in Latin, and these were some of Aristotle’s poorest works. By the middle of the thirteenth century, however, almost all of his existing books were translated from Arabic into Latin along with commentaries from Islamic thinkers like Avicenna and, most importantly, Averroes. In fact, Averroes became the primary guide to Aristotle to the degree that where Aristotle was spoken of as ‘The Philosopher’, Averroes was known as ‘The Commentator’. On the basis of Averroes’ writings, a trend of radical Aristotelianism began to develop amongst the Schoolmen.

zh: 这些新发掘的文献彻底革新了整个哲学和宗教思想，并导致了当时主流意识形态的全面危机。亚里士多德的科学探究方法与奥古斯丁的柏拉图式教条形成了鲜明对比。教会试图通过审查来摆脱这一困境。在1210年、1270 年和1277 年的谴责令中，教会列出了禁书和禁论清单，主要目的是审查亚里士多德的自然哲学以及阿威罗伊对亚里士多德思想的激进诠释。
en: This newly unearthed material revolutionised all of philosophy and religious thought, and led to a full-blown crisis within the prevailing ideology. The scientific and inquisitive method of Aristotle stood in sharp contrast to Augustine’s Platonic dogmas. The Church attempted to censor its way out of this. In the condemnations of 1210, 1270 and 1277, lists of forbidden books and theses were drawn up, mainly as an attempt to censor Aristotle’s natural philosophy and the radical interpretation of Aristotle by Averroes.

zh: 但教会无法阻挡历史的进程。阿伯拉尔的认识论此时已被普遍接受，并因亚里士多德思想的重新发现而得到支持。随着科学缓慢的进步，奥古斯丁学说中的漏洞开始日益显现。在此背景下，阿威罗伊主义迅速扩大影响。因此，一种试图融合柏拉图主义与亚里士多德主义世界观的思潮应运而生，旨在对抗阿威罗伊对亚里士多德的激进诠释。
en: But the Church could not stop the march of history. Abelard’s theory of knowledge was now universally accepted and backed up by the rediscovery of Aristotle. Along with the slow advance of science, bigger and bigger gaps were beginning to appear in the Augustinian approach. In this context, Averroism was rapidly gaining ground. Therefore, a trend emerged trying to merge the Platonic and Aristotelian world views, in order to combat the radical Averroist interpretation of Aristotle.

zh: 这一思潮最杰出的代表是托马斯·阿奎那（1225—1274），他或许是中世纪最著名的经院哲学家。阿奎那不得不承认，对普遍概念的认识是通过感官经验获得的，随后由心灵进行抽象。然而，他坚持认为，这种抽象能力是灵魂的功能，灵魂从上帝那里获得了“理智之光”，从而能够理解共相。阿奎那认为，通过这种方式，可以调和亚里士多德的唯物主义与柏拉图的唯心主义之间的矛盾。当然，实际上，他是在篡改亚里士多德的思想，并利用这些思想来维护教会的柏拉图主义。
en: The most prominent representative of this trend was Thomas Aquinas (1225-1274), perhaps the most famous mediaeval scholastic. Aquinas had to admit that knowledge of universal concepts is acquired via sense experience, which the mind then abstracts. However, he maintained that this ability to abstract is a function of the soul, which has been provided with intelligible light by God in order to be able to understand universals. In this manner, Aquinas believed that the contradiction between Aristotle’s materialism and Plato’s idealism could be reconciled. In reality of course, he was bastardising Aristotle’s ideas and using them to save the Platonism of the Church.

zh: 他还承认，世界中只有个别存在物，但这些存在物是由物质与独立的普遍本质组合而成的，而只有理性——无需借助经验——才能理解这种普遍本质。同样，阿奎那认为这将使在欧洲日益兴起的科学方法与古老传统相协调。但实际上，阿奎那仍然是一个实在论者，他的思想只不过是试图支撑当时的主流思想。
en: He also admitted that the world is only inhabited by singular beings, but that these are composed of a combination of matter, as well as a separate universal essence, which only reason – without recourse to experience – is able to understand. Again, Aquinas believed that this would reconcile the scientific approach, which was gaining traction in Europe with the old tradition. But in effect, Aquinas remained a Realist and his ideas were merely an attempt at propping up the ruling ideas of the time.

zh: 起初，阿奎那遭到了许多教会精英的敌视。然而后来，随着科学进步日益揭露旧有观点的谬误，教会不得不让步，将托马斯主义——即阿奎那的哲学——纳入其正统教义。奥古斯丁思想注定要消亡。因此，阿奎那的思想便成了以准科学外衣兜售旧教条的最佳途径。事实上，时至今日，新托马斯主义仍是罗马天主教会的基本立场。
en: At first, Aquinas was met with hostility by many of the ecclesiastic elite. Later on, however, as the advances of science increasingly exposed the old views, the Church had to concede and incorporate Thomism – as Aquinas’ philosophy was called – into its canon. Augustinian thought was doomed to perish. Aquinas’ ideas thus became the best way to sell the old dogma in a quasi-scientific guise. To this day in fact, neo-Thomism remains a basic position of the Roman Catholic Church.

zh: 为反对阿奎那，苏格兰哲学家约翰·邓斯·司各脱（1265—1308）提出了“存在的一义性”理论。所谓“一义性”，是指仅具有一种含义的特性，该理论主张：我们用来描述自然世界的那些命题，同样可以用来论述上帝。这与官方教义相悖，后者声称上帝与我们用来描述他的命题属于截然不同的领域。本质上，司各脱的观点暗示，上帝与其他受造物之间的差异仅仅是程度上的问题。马克思曾这样评价司各脱：
en: In opposing Aquinas, Scottish philosopher John Duns Scotus (1265-1308) developed the theory of the Univocity of Being. Univocity means the quality of only possessing one meaning, which maintains that the same propositions that we use about the natural world can also be used to speak about God. This went against the official doctrine, which claimed that God and the propositions we apply to him belong to an entirely different realm. Essentially, what Scotus’ view was hinting at was that the difference between God and other creatures is merely a matter of degree. Marx said of Scotus:

zh: 唯物主义是英国的嫡出之子。就连英国伟大的经院哲学家之一邓斯·司各脱，也曾自问“物质是否不能思考”。为了实现这一奇迹，邓斯诉诸了上帝的全能，也就是说，他让神学本身宣扬了唯物主义。
en: Materialism is the born son of Britain. Even one of his great schoolmen, Duns Scotus, asked himself “whether matter cannot think.” In performing this wonder, Duns had recourse to God’s omnipotence, that is, he made theology itself preach materialism.

zh: 这种观点在许多方面可视为斯宾诺莎后来所发展的泛神论的早期预兆。
en: This outlook is in many ways an early anticipation of the Pantheism later developed by Spinoza.

zh: 最后一位重要的经院哲学家是奥卡姆的威廉（1287—1347），他将阿伯拉尔开创的唯名论发展到了极致。与其他唯名论者一样，他坚持认为世界仅由个别事物构成，其中没有普遍实体的容身之地。事实上，他甚至将实在论关于共相的立场斥为“哲学中最严重的谬误”。
相反，奥卡姆认为共相仅仅是人类心灵基于经验形成的概念。因此，根据奥卡姆的观点，当我说“人”时，我只不过是在谈论自己通过所有关于人的经验所形成的概念。正是基于这些经验，科学才能确立普遍真理。
en: The last of the important Schoolmen was William of Ockham (1287-1347), who developed Nominalism – the school of thought inaugurated by Abelard – to its fullest. Like other Nominalists, he maintained that the world is only populated by singular elements, and that there is no room in it for universal entities. In fact, he went as far as to denounce Realism’s position on universals as “the worst error in philosophy”.

Instead, Ockham held that universals were merely concepts of the human mind solely based on our experiences. Thus, when I say ‘man’, according to Ockham, I am merely speaking about the concept I have developed through all of my experiences of men. It is on the basis of such experiences that science can establish universal truths.

zh: 奥卡姆还坚持认为，上帝的存在及其他宗教教条无法通过理性证明，因此完全建立在信仰之上。这是一种危险的学说，因为它意味着将哲学与宗教分离，使其得以摆脱教会的束缚而独立发展。1328 年，奥卡姆被教会开除教籍，但他逃离了教皇位于阿维尼翁的领地，投奔了同样被开除教籍的法国国王路易寻求庇护。随后，路易向大公会议提出上诉，结果教皇反而被指控为异端。据说，当奥卡姆见到神圣罗马帝国皇帝时，他对皇帝说道：“您用剑来保卫我，我就用笔来保卫您？”归根结底，这并非一场关于哲学的抽象辩论，而是教会与皇帝之间、法国、英格兰与德国之间生死搏斗的反映。围绕看似抽象观念的斗争本身，就是十三世纪——甚至在黑死病爆发之前——就已显现的封建秩序总体危机的一部分。
en: Ockham also maintained that the existence of God and other religious dogmas could not be proven by reason, and was thus founded solely upon faith. This was a dangerous doctrine, since it would mean separating philosophy from religion, enabling it to develop separately, freed from the dead hand of the Church. Ockham was excommunicated in 1328, but escaped from the Pope’s territory in Avignon and fled to the protection of Louis, King of France, who was also excommunicated. Louis then appealed to a general Council, and the Pope found himself accused of heresy. It is said that when Ockham met the Holy Roman Emperor, he said to him: “Do you defend me with the sword, and I will defend you with the pen?”. At bottom, this was not an abstract debate about philosophy, but the reflection of a life and death struggle between the Church and Emperor, and between France, England and Germany. The struggle over seemingly abstract ideas was itself part of the general crisis of the feudal order that had emerged in the thirteenth century, even prior to the Black Death.
body.review: 本段原文先写“Louis, King of France”（法国国王路易），后又称“Holy Roman Emperor”（神圣罗马帝国皇帝）。两种称谓均按原文保留，未静默统一。

zh: 虽然唯名论哲学蕴含着正确唯物主义思想的萌芽，但它走得太远，认为一般概念（“共相”）仅仅是名称，除此之外别无其他。事实上，它们反映了客观存在事物的真实属性；这些事物除了其特殊特征外，自身还蕴含着普遍性的要素，正是这些要素使它们被归入特定的属或种。这些并非超自然的普遍特征，而是反映自然本身普遍规律的特征。这种对普遍性的否定和对个别性的执着，是经验主义思维方式的独特特征，此后这一特征一直贯穿于盎格鲁-撒克逊哲学传统之中。作为对中世纪教会那些贫瘠的唯心主义学说的反拨，它代表了一次重要的进步——是朝着科学实验方向迈出的一步。
en: While containing the germ of a correct materialist idea, the philosophy of Nominalism went too far in assuming that general concepts (‘universals’) are only names, and nothing else. In fact, they reflect real qualities of objectively existing things, which, apart from their particular features, also embody within themselves elements of the general, which identify them as belonging to a specific genus or species. These are not supernatural general features, but features reflecting the general lawfulness of nature itself. This denial of the general and insistence on particulars is a peculiar feature of the empirical cast of mind, which has characterised the Anglo-Saxon philosophical tradition ever since. As a reaction against the sterile idealist doctrines of the medieval Church, it represented an important advance – a step in the direction of scientific experiment.

zh: 唯名论蕴含着唯物主义的萌芽，但这是一种片面且肤浅的唯物主义，后来在贝克莱、休谟以及现代语义哲学家那里走入了哲学死胡同。然而，在当时，它代表了一次巨大的进步。奥卡姆是最后一位伟大的经院哲学家，但他的思想方法鼓舞了一代新思想家，他们后来在科学领域取得了重要发现。实际上，奥卡姆的唯名论为经院哲学本身敲响了最后的丧钟。从这一刻起，科学与哲学便踏上了与神学截然不同的道路。
en: Nominalism contained the germ of materialism, but a one-sided and superficial materialism which later led to a philosophical dead-end with Berkeley, Hume and the modern semantic philosophers. At the time, however, it represented a huge advance. Ockham was the last of the great Schoolmen, but his approach encouraged a new generation of thinkers who would make important discoveries in science. In reality, Ockham’s Nominalism represented the last nail in the coffin of scholasticism as such. From this point, science and philosophy embarked upon a distinctly separate path from theology.

zh: 尽管中世纪经院哲学家中确实不乏杰出的思想家，但由于教会强加的官方教条，他们的成就受到限制。即使是当时最伟大的思想家的著作，也蒙上了宗教神秘主义的阴影。因此，总体而言，经院哲学并未超越古希腊哲学的成就。尽管如此，它在恢复过去的进步方面发挥了重要作用，为文艺复兴时期的进步奠定了基础。
en: While the medieval Schoolmen did have among them brilliant thinkers, they were limited in what they could achieve due to the official dogma imposed by the Church. Even the works of the greatest minds of the time were clouded by religious mysticism. Hence, in the main, scholastic philosophy did not go beyond the achievements of classical Greek philosophy. Nevertheless, it played an important role in recovering the advances of the past, setting the stage for the advances made during the Renaissance.

zh: 科学与宗教的对抗
en: SCIENCE VS. RELIGION

zh: 在此之前的数百年间，科学的进步一直受到教会“精神警察”的扼杀。经院哲学家们大部分（且非同小可）的智力精力，都耗费在关于“天使的性别”等主题的无休止且复杂的辩论中。任何人都不被允许超越教会教条规定的界限，而那些试图越界者则会面临严厉的报复。但这种局面开始走向终结。罗伯特·格罗斯泰斯特、大阿尔伯特以及后来让·布里丹等人，也对科学的发展以及基于观察和实验的科学方法的普及作出了贡献。
en: For hundreds of years prior to this, the progress of science had been stifled by the spiritual police of the Church. Most of the (not inconsiderable) intellectual energies of the Schoolmen were dissipated in endless and complicated debates on such subjects as the sex of angels. Nobody was permitted to go beyond the limits laid down by Church dogma, and those who attempted to do so left themselves open to harsh reprisals. But that was beginning to come to an end. People like Roberte Grosseteste, Albert the Great and, later on, Jean Buridan also made important contributions to the proliferation of science and the scientific method of observation and experimentation.

zh: 尽管如此，当英国经院哲学家罗杰·培根（约1214—1292 年）竟敢挑战经院哲学家的教条主义和对权威的崇拜时，这仍需要极大的勇气。他逆时代潮流而行，预见了科学方法，主张对自然进行实验研究。鉴于当时科学尚未与炼金术和占星术完全分离，培根的著作中出现这些元素也就不足为奇了。同样不足为奇的是，他因这种大胆而“获得”了“奖励”——因持异端观点被解除了牛津大学的教职，并被囚禁于修道院。考虑到当时的情况，他的下场还算轻了。
en: Nevertheless, it called for great courage when the English scholastic Roger Bacon (c. 1214-92) went so far as to challenge the Schoolmen’s dogmatism and veneration of authority. Going against the spirit of the times, and anticipating the scientific method, he advocated the experimental study of nature. Given the fact that science had still not separated itself from alchemy and astrology, it is not surprising that elements of these were present in Bacon’s writings. Nor is it surprising that he was rewarded for his boldness by being dismissed from teaching at Oxford and confined to a monastery for his heretical views. Given the circumstances, he got off lightly.

zh: 奥雷姆的尼古拉是奥卡姆的学生，他比哥白尼更早地探讨了以地球为宇宙中心的“地心说”。他将这一观点与主张太阳位于宇宙中心的日心说进行比较后得出结论：这两种理论都能解释所有已知的事实，因此无法在二者之间做出选择。这一看似谨慎的结论实际上却是一个相当大胆的举措，因为它对教会的正统立场打上了问号，从而挑战了教会的整个世界观。
en: Nicholas of Oresme, a pupil of Ockham’s, anticipated Copernicus by considering the geocentric theory of the universe, which places the Earth at the centre of the universe. Comparing this idea with the heliocentric theory, which states that the sun is at the centre, he concluded that either theory would serve to explain all the known facts, and that, therefore, it was impossible to choose between them. This apparently cautious conclusion was, in fact, quite a bold step, since it put a question mark over the orthodox position of the Church, and thereby challenged its whole world outlook.

zh: 中世纪教会的宇宙论是其整体世界观的重要组成部分，绝非次要问题。宇宙图景被视为世界的镜像，具有同样的静态、一成不变的特征，以及同样僵化的等级制度。它并非源于观察，而是承袭自亚里士多德和亚历山大里亚学派的宇宙论，并被教条式地接受。伯纳尔评论道：
en: The cosmology of the medieval Church formed an important part of its general world outlook. It was not a secondary issue. The picture of the universe was supposed to be a mirror image of the world, with the same kind of static, unchanging character, the same rigid hierarchy. It was not derived from observation, but taken over from the cosmology of Aristotle and the Alexandrines, and accepted dogmatically. Bernal comments:

zh: 社会等级制度在宇宙等级体系中得到了再现；正如世上有教皇、主教和大主教，有皇帝、国王和贵族，天界也有由九品天使组成的等级体系：炽天使、智天使、座天使；主天使、力天使和能天使；权天使、大天使和天使（这些全是伪狄奥尼修斯想象力的产物）。这些天使在宇宙的运转中各自承担着明确的职能，并按应有的等级隶属于各行星天球，以维持其恰当的运动。隶属于月球天球的最低阶普通天使，自然与紧随其下的人类秩序关系最为密切。总体而言，存在着宇宙秩序、社会秩序以及人体内部的秩序，它们都代表着自然界在受到扰动时倾向于回归的状态。万物皆有其位，万物皆知其位置。
en: The hierarchy of society was reproduced in the hierarchy of the universe itself; just as there was the pope, bishops, and archbishops, the emperor, kings, and nobles, so there was a celestial hierarchy of the nine choirs of angels: seraphim, cherubim, thrones; dominations, virtues, and powers; principalities, archangels, and angels (all fruits of the imagination of the pseudo Dionysius). Each of these had a definite function to perform in the running of the universe, and they were attached in due rank to the planetary spheres to keep them in appropriate motion. The lowest order of mere angels that belonged to the sphere of the moon had naturally most to do with the order of human beings just below them. In general there was a cosmic order, a social order, an order inside the human body, all representing states to which Nature tended to return when it was disturbed. There was a place for everything and everything knew its place.

zh: 若要挑战这种宇宙观，就不得不质疑教会的整个世界观及其所捍卫的社会形态。围绕哥白尼和伽利略思想的冲突，并非一场抽象的智力辩论，而是两种对立世界观之间的生死之战，这最终反映了两种相互排斥的社会秩序之间的殊死搏斗。
en: This view of the universe could not be challenged without calling into question the entire world outlook of the Church, and the type of society it defended. The conflict around the ideas of Copernicus and Galileo was not an abstract intellectual debate, but a life-and-death battle between opposing views of the world, which ultimately reflected a desperate struggle between two mutually exclusive social orders.

zh: 资产阶级的兴起
en: THE RISE OF THE BOURGEOISIE

zh: 在中世纪后期，随着城镇和贸易的兴起，社会格局中出现了一股崭新而充满活力的力量。这一发展具有不均衡的特征。有些地区的增长速度快于其他地区。托尼揭示了新社会的胚胎如何在旧社会的子宫中逐渐成长：
en: In the later Middle Ages, the rise of the towns and trade saw the emergence of a new and vigorous element in the social equation. This development had an uneven character. Some regions grew faster than others. Tawney shows how the embryo of a new society was growing within the womb of the old:

zh: 尽管庄园和行会无处不在，但像15 世纪的佛兰德斯这样的资本主义工业中心，或像15 世纪的佛罗伦萨这样的资本主义金融中心，与像中世纪英格兰那样出口原材料和少量粮食的牧业社会之间的差异，就如同现代的兰开夏郡或伦敦与现代的丹麦之间的差异一样。
en: In spite of the ubiquity of manor and gild, there was as much difference between the life of a centre of capitalist industry, like fifteenth-century Flanders, or a centre of capitalist finance, like fifteenth-century Florence, and a pastoral society exporting raw materials and a little food, like medieval England, as there is between modern Lancashire or London and modern Denmark.

zh: 在此背景下，新兴的富裕商人阶层开始展现实力，要求获得相应权利。商业的扩张、新贸易路线的开辟、货币经济的兴起、新需求的产生及其满足手段的创造、艺术与手工业的发展、新民族文学的兴起：所有这些发展都预示着社会中一股革命力量——资产阶级的诞生。其利益不仅在于打破阻碍其发展的人为封建壁垒，而且在日益加剧的程度上，还在于发展和利用技术创新。
en: In this context, the rising class of wealthy merchants began to flex its muscles, demanding rights. The expansion of commerce, the opening up of new trade routes, the rise of a money economy, the creation of new needs and the means of satisfying them, the development of arts and crafts, the rise of a new national literature: all these developments heralded the birth of a revolutionary force in society, the bourgeoisie, whose interests laid in breaking down the artificial feudal barriers which impeded its development, and also, to an ever-increasing extent, in developing and exploiting technical innovations.

zh: 例如，远洋航行的发展要求制作基于精确天文观测的新型、更精确的海图，以及更先进的导航仪器。纸张和印刷术的引入对思想的传播产生了革命性的影响——此前，这些思想仅限于极少数神职人员。首次出现用本土语言创作的文学作品也产生了同样的影响，薄伽丘、但丁、拉伯雷、乔叟以及最终的路德等杰出的、具有民族代表性的作家相继涌现。火药的引入不仅彻底改变了战争形态并有助于削弱贵族的权力，还为物理学和化学的研究注入了新的动力。
en: The development of open-sea navigation, for example, demanded the production of new and better charts, based on accurate astronomical observations, and also of more advanced navigational instruments. The introduction of paper and printing had a revolutionary effect on the accessibility of ideas, which had earlier been limited to a tiny minority of ecclesiastics. The production of literature written in the vernacular for the first time had the same effect, with the emergence of great recognisable national writers like Boccaccio, Dante, Rabelais, Chaucer and, finally, Luther. The introduction of gunpowder not only revolutionised warfare and helped undermine the power of the nobles, but also gave a new impetus to the study of physics and chemistry.

zh: 先是在意大利，随后在低地国家、英国、波希米亚、德国和法国，这个新兴阶层开始挑战旧秩序——该秩序在延续近千年后已日渐衰竭，进入了一个衰落阶段。这一时期无休止的战争和内战，印证了封建制度的僵局。十四世纪席卷欧洲、导致人口锐减的黑死病，加速了土地上封建关系的瓦解。法国的雅克里起义和1381 年英格兰的农民起义，预示着封建秩序即将瓦解。在许多人看来，世界末日似乎近在眼前。这种末日将至的预感催生了“自鞭教派”等现象——这些宗教狂热分子游走全国各地，通过鞭打等自虐行为来迎接即将到来的“审判日”。这不过是民众在面对现有社会秩序即将瓦解时，在想象中产生的混乱反映罢了。
en: First in Italy, then in the Low Countries, Britain, Bohemia, Germany and France, this new class began to challenge the old order, which, after nearly a thousand years, had exhausted itself and entered a phase of decline. The endless wars and civil wars of the period bore witness to the impasse of feudalism. The Black Death, which decimated the population of Europe in the fourteenth century, hastened the dissolution of feudal relations on the land. The peasant jacqueries in France and the Peasant Rising in England in 1381 were a warning of the approaching dissolution of the feudal order. To many people, it seemed that the end of the world was approaching. The sensation of impending doom gave rise to phenomena like the flagellant sects, groups of religious fanatics who travelled the country, whipping and otherwise inflicting pain on themselves in anticipation of the impending Day of Wrath. This was merely a confused reflection in the popular imagination of the impending break-up of the existing social order.

zh: 意识形态危机
en: CRISIS OF IDEOLOGY

zh: 官方道德与意识形态的危机预示着社会制度的崩溃，二者与已经变化的社会关系之间的冲突日益加剧。一部分知识分子中开始涌现批判精神，这成为社会深层日益加剧的紧张局势的晴雨表。封建制度的道德和意识形态基础是教会的教义。任何对现有秩序的严重挑战都意味着对教会的攻击，而教会则动用一切手段捍卫其权力和特权，包括绝罚、酷刑和火刑。
en: The breakdown of a social system is anticipated by a crisis of the official morality and ideology, which increasingly enters into conflict with the changed social relations. A critical spirit arises among a layer of the intellectuals, a barometer of the tensions building up within the depths of society. The moral and ideological basis for the feudal system was the teaching of the Church. Any serious challenge to the existing order meant an assault on the Church, which defended its power and privileges with all the means at its disposal, including excommunication, torture and burning at the stake.

zh: 中世纪通常被描绘为一个宗教虔诚与敬神之情极盛的时代。但这种描述显然不适用于我们正在探讨的这一时期。教会作为一个富庶而强大的机构，给社会带来了沉重负担，其声誉已广受质疑。赫伊津哈写道：
en: The Middle Ages are usually depicted as a time of extreme religious devotion and piety. But that description certainly does not apply to the period under consideration. The Church, a wealthy and powerful institution which weighed heavily on the back of society, was widely discredited. Huizinga writes:

zh: 在那个时代宗教生活所呈现的所有矛盾中，或许最难以调和的，便是对神职人员的公然蔑视——这种蔑视被视为贯穿整个中世纪的一股暗流，与人们对神职的神圣性所表现出的极大尊重并存……正因如此，贵族、市民和农奴们长期以来一直通过嘲讽放纵的修士和暴饮暴食的教士，以此来滋养他们的仇恨。在此语境下，“仇恨”一词用得恰如其分，因为这确实是仇恨——虽是潜藏的，却普遍而持久。民众听闻神职人员的恶行被控诉，却从未感到厌倦。任何抨击教会现状的布道者都必定会赢得掌声。锡耶纳的伯纳迪诺指出，一旦讲道者触及这一话题，听众便会忘却其他一切；当会众开始打瞌睡，或因酷热或严寒而苦恼时，再没有比这更有效的唤醒注意力的手段了。每个人都会立刻聚精会神，心情愉悦。
en: Of all the contradictions which religious life of the period presents, perhaps the most insoluble is that of an avowed contempt of the clergy, a contempt seen as an undercurrent throughout the Middle Ages, side by side with the very great respect shown for the sanctity of the sacerdotal office … Hence it was that nobles, burghers and villeins had for a long time past been feeding their hatred with spiteful jests at the expense of the incontinent monk and the guzzling priest. Hatred is the right word to use in this context, for hatred it was, latent, but general and persistent. The people never wearied of hearing the vices of the clergy arraigned. A preacher who inveighed against the ecclesiastical state was sure of being applauded. As soon as a homilist broaches this subject, says Bernardino of Siena, his hearers forget all the rest; there is no more effective means of reviving attention when the congregation is dropping off to sleep, or suffering from heat or cold. Everybody instantly becomes attentive and cheerful.

zh: 就连教会内部也感受到了异议的暗流，这反映了社会施加的压力。阿尔比派等异端运动遭到了血腥镇压。但新的反对思潮接踵而至，有时还伪装成神秘主义的外衣。一位十九世纪的意大利历史学家写道：
en: The undercurrents of dissent were felt even within the Church itself, reflecting the pressures of society. Heretical movements like the Albigenses were put down in blood. But new oppositional trends appeared, sometimes disguised in the garb of mysticism. A nineteenth century Italian historian relates:

zh: 曾激励阿尔比派的同一股改革精神已蔓延至整个欧洲：许多基督徒因厌恶神职人员的腐败与恶习，或因内心反抗教会对理性的压制，便投身于静修生活，摒弃一切野心与世俗享乐，并试图通过将信仰与理性相结合，寻求一条通往救赎的新道路。他们自称“卡塔尔派”（cathari），即“净化者”；或称“帕特里尼派”（paterini），即“超脱者”。
en: The same spirit of reformation which animated the Albigenses had spread throughout Europe: many Christians, disgusted with the corruption and vices of the clergy, or whose minds revolted against the violence on their reason exercised by the church, devoted themselves to a contemplative life, renounced all ambition and the pleasures of the world, and sought a new road to salvation in the alliance of faith with reason. They called themselves cathari, or the purified; paterini, or the resigned.

zh: 多明我会和方济各会成立于十二世纪初，旨在打击异端、反教权主义以及新的哲学思想。西斯蒙迪在谈到教皇英诺森三世时说：
en: The Dominican and Franciscan orders were founded in the early twelfth century to combat heresies, anti-clericalism and new philosophical ideas. Sismondi says of Pope Innocent the Third:

zh: 他创立了方济各会和多明我会这两个乞食修会；这些作为教会新卫士的修会，被赋予了压制一切思想活动、对抗日益增长的智慧以及铲除异端的使命。他将自己设立的宗教裁判所那骇人的权力托付给了多明我会：他命令他们查出并追捕至灭绝那些以“帕特里尼派”之名在意大利迅速蔓延的新改革者。
en: He founded the two mendicant orders of Franciscans and Dominicans; new champions of the church, who were charged to repress all activity of mind, to combat growing intelligence, and to extirpate heresy. He confided to the Dominicans the fearful powers of the inquisition, which he instituted: he charged them to discover and pursue to destruction the new reformers, who, under the name of paterini, multiplied rapidly in Italy.

zh: 正如教皇制的历史所显示的那样，对任何形式的反对意见进行暴力镇压，一直是最高层教会当局行为中的一贯特征。教皇乌尔班六世在无法获得枢机主教们支持时，仅凭指控他们密谋反对自己这一简单手段便解决了问题。他让许多枢机主教在他面前遭受酷刑，而他却若无其事地诵念着玫瑰经。他还下令将其他人装进麻袋，扔进海里淹死。改革派修士吉罗拉莫·萨沃纳罗拉——这位意大利的“路德先驱”——遭受了酷刑，直到他供认了被强加的所有罪行，随后与另外两名修士一同被活活烧死。此类例子不胜枚举。
en: Violent repression of opposition of any kind was a constant feature of the conduct of the ecclesiastical authorities from the highest level, as the history of the papacy shows. Pope Urban the Sixth, when he could not get the support of his cardinals, resolved the problem by the simple expedient of accusing them of conspiracy against him. He had many cardinals put to the torture in his presence, while he calmly recited his rosary. Others he ordered to be put in sacks and drowned in the sea. The reforming monk Girolamo Savonarola, an Italian precursor of Luther, was tortured until he confessed all the crimes attributed to him, and burnt alive with two other monks. Examples can be multiplied at will.

zh: 但无论多么严厉的镇压，都无法维系一种已经过时的思想。一种不再反映现实的意识形态和道德观，已经过时，注定会被推翻。历史上一场最伟大的革命的土壤已然形成。1517 年10 月31 日，一位名叫马丁·路德的默默无闻的修士将他的《九十五条论纲》钉在维滕贝格诸圣教堂的大门上，他点燃的导火索将旧的封建秩序炸得粉碎，为一个新时代——资产阶级革命时代——拉开了序幕。
en: But no amount of repression can preserve an idea whose time has passed. An ideology and morality which no longer reflects reality is one that has outlived itself and is destined to be overthrown. The ground was prepared for one of the greatest revolutions in history. When, on 31 October 1517, an obscure monk called Martin Luther nailed his ninety-five theses to the door of All Saints’ Church in Wittenberg, he lit a fuse that blew the old feudal order sky-high, opening the door to a new epoch – the age of the bourgeois revolution.
